guides.title: Lost money to investment fraud? What to do first
guides.summary: Investment fraud covers Ponzi schemes, fake funds, unauthorised trading, mis-sold products and advisers who misrepresented risk. The steps you take in the first weeks often decide whether money can still be traced and recovered.

guides.title: Crypto scam recovery: first steps and how lawyers trace funds
guides.summary: Crypto transfers are public on the blockchain, which means funds can sometimes be followed to an exchange where an account holder can be identified. Speed matters: once funds are moved through mixers or off-ramped, options narrow.

guides.title: Property and off-plan fraud: how to protect your claim
guides.summary: Property fraud ranges from fake listings and diverted deposits to off-plan developments that never complete and title problems discovered after purchase. Your contracts and payment records are the foundation of any claim.

guides.title: Client won't pay? A guide to recovering unpaid invoices
guides.summary: Most unpaid invoices are resolved without court, but a structured approach, and acting before the debtor's position worsens, improves your chances.

guides.title: When a business partner takes the money: your options
guides.summary: Partnership and shareholder disputes often start with exclusion from information and end with diverted revenue, dilution or asset stripping. Acting early protects both evidence and value.

guides.title: Romance and pig-butchering scams: what victims can do
guides.summary: Romance scams build trust over weeks or months, often before introducing an “investment” platform. Victims are not at fault, these are organised operations. There are practical steps that can still help.

guides.title: Insurance claim denied? How to challenge it
guides.summary: Insurers reject claims for many reasons, exclusions, late notification, alleged non-disclosure or disputes about the value of the loss. Many rejections can be challenged.

guides.title: Bad advice from a professional? Claiming for negligence
guides.summary: Professionals owe a duty to act with reasonable skill and care. When they fall short and it causes a financial loss, you may have a claim, usually against their professional indemnity insurance.

guides.title: Claims against Ryanair: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)
UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)

guides.summary: Ryanair is an Irish airline, so its flights from or to the EU are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, and flights from the UK by UK261. Most passenger claims against it are about long delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage. This guide explains how those claims usually work.

guides.title: Claims against Vueling: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Vueling is a Spanish airline, so its flights are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004. Passenger claims against it are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections, refunds and baggage. In Spain, the aviation safety agency AESA handles passenger complaints.

guides.title: Claims against easyJet: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)
Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: easyJet operates through a UK company and separate European companies, so a flight can fall under the EU rules (EU261) or the UK rules (UK261) depending on the route and the operating carrier. Passenger claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

guides.title: Claims against Lufthansa: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Lufthansa is a German airline, so its flights are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, including long-haul flights departing from the EU. Passenger claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections, refunds and baggage. In Germany, independent conciliation bodies handle passenger disputes free of charge for passengers.

guides.title: Claims against Iberia: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Iberia is a Spanish airline, so its flights are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, including long-haul flights departing from Spain. Passenger claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections, refunds and baggage.

guides.title: Claims against Santander: mortgages, cards and Banco Popular

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Banco Santander is one of Spain's largest banks and acquired Banco Popular in 2017. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products, and former Banco Popular investors brought claims after Popular's 2017 resolution. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

guides.title: Claims against BBVA: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: BBVA is one of Spain's largest banks. It was among the banks in the case in which the Spanish Supreme Court first ruled on floor clauses in May 2013, and like other Spanish banks it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

guides.title: Claims against CaixaBank: mortgages, cards and former Bankia

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: CaixaBank is one of Spain's largest banks and absorbed Bankia in 2021, so it is now the counterparty for many claims that began against Bankia. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

guides.title: Claims against Volkswagen: the diesel emissions scandal

sources.label: Federal Court of Justice (BGH), VI ZR 252/19, 25 May 2020

guides.summary: In September 2015 Volkswagen admitted that software in some of its diesel engines, mainly the EA189 engine used across the VW, Audi, SEAT and Skoda brands, made the cars perform differently in emissions tests than on the road. Owners in many countries have since brought individual and group claims. This guide explains how those claims have generally worked.

guides.title: Claims against Mercedes-Benz: diesel emissions

sources.label: CJEU, Mercedes-Benz Group, case C-100/21

guides.summary: Owners of some Mercedes-Benz diesel cars have brought claims arguing that emissions controls worked differently on the road than in tests, for example through temperature-dependent settings. German authorities ordered recalls of some models, and the manufacturer has disputed that its vehicles contained unlawful defeat devices. This guide explains how these claims have generally worked.

guides.title: Claims against Air France: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Air France is France's flag carrier and part of the Air France-KLM group. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and also when they fly into the EU from elsewhere. Claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections on long-haul trips and refunds.

guides.title: Claims against KLM: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is the Dutch airline of the Air France-KLM group, with its hub at Amsterdam Schiphol. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and when they fly into the EU. Many claims concern connections through Amsterdam, where the delay at the final destination is what counts.

guides.title: Claims against British Airways: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)
UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)

guides.summary: British Airways is the UK's flag carrier and part of International Airlines Group (IAG). Flights from the UK, and BA flights into the UK, are covered by UK261, the UK copy of the EU rules with amounts in pounds; BA flights departing from the EU are covered by EU261. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

guides.title: Claims against Wizz Air: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)
UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)

guides.summary: Wizz Air is a low-cost airline headquartered in Hungary, with a separate UK company for many flights from the UK. Its flights from the EU are covered by EU261 and flights operated by its UK company from or to the UK by UK261. Claims are mostly about cancellations, long delays, refunds and extra charges.

guides.title: Claims against TAP Air Portugal: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: TAP Air Portugal is Portugal's flag carrier, with its hub in Lisbon and many routes to Brazil and Africa. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and when they fly into the EU, which includes flights from Brazil to Lisbon.

guides.title: Claims against ITA Airways: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: ITA Airways is the Italian airline that started flying in October 2021, when Alitalia stopped operating. It is a separate company from Alitalia, so claims about earlier Alitalia flights are not normally brought against ITA. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from or fly into the EU.

guides.title: Claims against Aer Lingus: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)
UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)

guides.summary: Aer Lingus is an Irish airline and part of International Airlines Group (IAG). Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU, and flights from the UK by UK261. Claims are mostly about cancellations, delays on transatlantic routes, refunds and baggage.

guides.title: Claims against Eurowings: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Eurowings is the low-cost airline of the Lufthansa Group, based in Germany. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage on short-haul European routes.

guides.title: Claims against SWISS: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Swiss International Air Lines (SWISS) is Switzerland's national airline and part of the Lufthansa Group. Switzerland applies Regulation 261/2004 under its air transport agreement with the EU, so SWISS flights from Swiss and EU airports are covered in the same way as an EU airline's.

guides.title: Claims against Austrian Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Austrian Airlines is Austria's national airline and part of the Lufthansa Group, with its hub in Vienna. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU. Claims are mostly about delays, missed connections through Vienna, cancellations and refunds.

guides.title: Claims against Brussels Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Brussels Airlines is Belgium's main airline and part of the Lufthansa Group, with its hub at Brussels Airport and many routes to Africa. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU.

guides.title: Claims against Volotea: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Volotea is a low-cost airline registered in Spain that mainly connects medium-sized European cities. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004. Claims are mostly about cancellations, schedule changes, long delays and refunds.

guides.title: Claims against Air Europa: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Air Europa is a Spanish airline based in Mallorca, with a hub in Madrid and many routes to Latin America. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and when they fly into the EU, including flights from Latin America to Madrid.

guides.title: Claims against Norwegian: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Norwegian Air Shuttle is a Norwegian low-cost airline. Norway applies Regulation 261/2004 as part of the European Economic Area, so Norwegian's flights are covered in the same way as an EU airline's. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations and refunds.

guides.title: Claims against Transavia: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Transavia is the low-cost airline of the Air France-KLM group, with a Dutch company and a French company (Transavia France). Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004. Which company operated your flight decides where you complain, so check the flight number and your booking.

guides.title: Claims against Jet2: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)
UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk)

guides.summary: Jet2.com is a UK leisure airline based in Leeds, often sold with Jet2holidays packages. Its flights from the UK are covered by UK261 and its flights from EU airports back to the UK by EU261. Package holidaymakers also have rights against the tour operator.

guides.title: Claims against SAS: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) is the airline of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, headquartered near Stockholm. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or EEA, or fly into it. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

guides.title: Claims against LOT Polish Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: LOT Polish Airlines is Poland's flag carrier, with its hub in Warsaw. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and when they fly into the EU, including long-haul flights to Warsaw.

guides.title: Claims against Turkish Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Turkish Airlines is Türkiye's flag carrier, with its hub in Istanbul. Because it is not an EU airline, Regulation 261/2004 covers its flights departing from an EU airport, but not its flights from Istanbul into the EU. Türkiye has its own air passenger rules for flights from Turkish airports.

guides.title: Claims against Bankinter: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Bankinter is a Spanish bank known for its mortgage and private banking business. Besides the mortgage terms common to Spanish banks, customers have brought claims over multi-currency mortgages (hipotecas multidivisa) linked to foreign currencies such as the Swiss franc or the yen. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

guides.title: Claims against Banco Sabadell: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Banco Sabadell is one of Spain's largest banks and took over Caja de Ahorros del Mediterráneo (CAM) in 2012, so it now answers many claims about CAM mortgages and products. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products.

guides.title: Claims against Unicaja: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Unicaja is a Spanish bank from Málaga that merged with Liberbank in 2021, after earlier absorbing Caja España-Duero. Customers of all these banks now bring their claims against Unicaja, mostly about mortgage terms and credit products.

guides.title: Claims against Ibercaja: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Ibercaja is a Spanish bank based in Zaragoza, created from a savings bank, which absorbed Caja3 in 2013. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over floor clauses, mortgage costs, IRPH-indexed mortgages and credit cards.

guides.title: Claims against Abanca: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Abanca is a Galician bank formed from the savings banks Caixa Galicia and Caixanova (later NCG Banco), which was among the banks in the case where the Spanish Supreme Court first ruled on floor clauses in May 2013. It now answers claims about NCG and the former savings banks' products.

guides.title: Claims against Kutxabank: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards

sources.label: CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15
CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH)
CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs)
Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario

guides.summary: Kutxabank is a Basque bank formed from the savings banks BBK, Kutxa and Caja Vital, and it owns Cajasur in Andalusia. Customers of these banks have brought consumer claims over floor clauses, mortgage costs, IRPH-indexed mortgages and credit products.

guides.title: Claims against PKO Bank Polski: Swiss franc mortgages

sources.label: CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18
CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21
Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman)

guides.summary: PKO Bank Polski is Poland's largest bank. It is one of the banks that hold Swiss franc mortgage portfolios, and many borrowers have brought claims about the exchange-rate clauses in those loans. This guide explains how those claims generally work.

guides.title: Claims against mBank: Swiss franc mortgages

sources.label: CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18
CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21
Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman)

guides.summary: mBank is a Polish bank majority-owned by Germany's Commerzbank. It sold mortgages indexed to the Swiss franc before the 2008 financial crisis and has faced a large number of claims from borrowers about the exchange-rate clauses.

guides.title: Claims against Bank Millennium: Swiss franc mortgages

sources.label: CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18
CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21
Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman)

guides.summary: Bank Millennium is a Polish bank majority-owned by Portugal's Millennium bcp. It sold Swiss franc indexed mortgages and has faced many borrower claims about the exchange-rate clauses, and it has offered settlements to convert loans into zlotys.

guides.title: Claims against Santander Bank Polska: Swiss franc mortgages

sources.label: CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18
CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21
Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman)

guides.summary: Santander Bank Polska, formerly Bank Zachodni WBK, is part of the Santander group. Borrowers with Swiss franc mortgages from the bank and from banks it took over have brought claims about the exchange-rate clauses.

guides.title: Claims against Daimler Truck: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Daimler Truck, the German maker of Mercedes-Benz trucks, was one of the manufacturers fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. Buyers of its trucks from 1997 to 2011 have claimed damages for the overcharge, alone or in group claims.

guides.title: Claims against MAN Truck & Bus: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: MAN, the German truck maker in the Traton group, took part in the trucks cartel but was not fined because it revealed the cartel to the European Commission. That immunity does not protect it from damages claims: buyers of MAN trucks have also claimed for the overcharge.

guides.title: Claims against Volvo Trucks: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: The Swedish Volvo group, which also owns Renault Trucks, was fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. Buyers of Volvo and Renault trucks from 1997 to 2011 have claimed damages, and the CJEU's 2022 ruling on limitation came from a Spanish case against Volvo and DAF.

guides.title: Claims against DAF Trucks: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: DAF, the Dutch truck maker owned by PACCAR, was fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. DAF buyers have brought many of the leading cases, including the Spanish case that reached the CJEU in 2022.

guides.title: Claims against Iveco: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Iveco, the Italian truck maker, was fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. Buyers of Iveco trucks from 1997 to 2011 have claimed damages for the overcharge in Italy, Spain and other countries.

guides.title: Claims against Scania: the trucks cartel

sources.label: European Commission: Scania decision, September 2017
CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Scania, the Swedish truck maker in the Traton group, did not settle with the European Commission and was fined separately in September 2017 for the same cartel. Its appeals were dismissed, and buyers of Scania trucks have claimed damages for the overcharge.

guides.title: Claims against Deutsche Bahn: train delays and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Deutsche Bahn is Germany's national rail operator. Its long-distance and regional trains are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and German law adds some rights for local transport. Claims are mostly about delays, missed connections and cancelled trains.

guides.title: Claims against SNCF Voyageurs: train delays and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: SNCF Voyageurs runs France's TGV INOUI, Ouigo, Intercités and regional trains. Its services are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and SNCF also has its own delay guarantees on some services. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations and strikes.

guides.title: Claims against Renfe: train delays and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Renfe is Spain's national rail operator, running AVE high-speed, long-distance and commuter trains. Its services are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and Renfe also publishes its own punctuality commitment, which on some services is more generous than the EU minimum.

guides.title: Claims against Trenitalia: train delays and refunds

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Trenitalia is Italy's main rail operator, running Frecce high-speed, Intercity and regional trains. Its services are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations and missed connections.

guides.title: Claims against Google: competition damages (Google Shopping)

sources.label: CJEU, Google and Alphabet v Commission, case C-48/22 P (Google Shopping)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: In June 2017 the European Commission fined Google for favouring its own comparison shopping service in search results. The General Court upheld the decision in 2021 and the Court of Justice of the EU dismissed Google's final appeal in September 2024 (case C-48/22 P). Price comparison sites and other businesses have since claimed damages in national courts.

guides.title: Claims against Booking.com: parity clauses and hotel claims

sources.label: CJEU, Booking.com, case C-264/23 (parity clauses)
Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex)

guides.summary: Booking.com, based in Amsterdam, used price parity clauses that stopped hotels offering lower prices elsewhere. In September 2024 the Court of Justice of the EU ruled (case C-264/23) that such clauses are not, in principle, an ancillary restraint exempt from competition law. Hotels in several countries have since brought or announced damages claims.
